text: If you stopped sleeping, after just one day, tiny parts of your brain would start falling asleep... while you're still awake.
These are called microsleeps. For a few seconds, your brain simply switches off, and you don't even notice.
After twenty-four hours awake, your reaction time is about as bad as someone who's legally drunk.
That's because while you sleep, your brain runs a cleaning system that washes away the waste built up during the day. Skip sleep, and the trash piles up.
Your body gets confused too. The hormone that makes you hungry goes up, and the one that tells you you're full goes down. So you crave junk food.
Your immune system gets weaker, which makes it easier to catch a cold.
By day three, many people start seeing things that aren't there: walls that seem to move, and shapes in the corner of their eye.
But here's the crazy part. In 1964, a seventeen-year-old named Randy Gardner stayed awake for eleven whole days.
By the end, he struggled to remember things and even hallucinated. It became so risky that Guinness World Records stopped accepting attempts.
So tonight, put the phone down. Sleep isn't wasted time... it's when your brain repairs itself.
